database_summary: E‑commerce dataset with customers, sellers, products, orders, order-level payments and reviews, order_items (line items), geolocation and product category translations. Additional marketing/CRM leads tables (leads_qualified, leads_closed) capture acquisition and closed leads. Mix of current-entity tables (sellers, customers, products) and event/history tables (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews, geolocation rows as measurements). Useful for order-level revenue, fulfillment and review analytics and joining to customer/seller geography and product categories.

accepted.name: order_items_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english
FROM order_items AS oi
LEFT JOIN orders AS o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN customers AS c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN sellers AS s
  ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
LEFT JOIN products AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation AS t
  ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
accepted.description: One row per order_items line enriched with order header, customer and seller attributes plus product category translation. Useful for revenue, fulfillment, product- and geography-level analyses where line-item-level measures are needed. | Use for: calculate order-line revenue, average price or freight by product category or geography; join reviews/payments to line items for per-line profitability; analyze seller performance by delivered orders and revenue

accepted.name: order_payments_aggregated
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total,
  MIN(payment_value) AS payment_value_min,
  MAX(payment_value) AS payment_value_max
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: One row per order with aggregated payment metrics: total payment_value, count of payment rows, and breakdown metrics helpful to reconcile payments to order totals or to examine payment method usage. Use when comparing order-level amounts or joining to orders/order_items. | Use for: compare aggregated payments to order line totals to find mismatches; identify orders with multiple payment attempts or split payments; compute revenue per order after aggregating payment rows

accepted.name: orders_with_review
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date,
  r.review_id,
  r.review_score,
  r.review_creation_date
FROM orders AS o
LEFT JOIN order_reviews AS r
  ON o.order_id = r.order_id
accepted.description: One row per order enriched with review information when present (left join). Useful to analyze how review_score relates to order attributes, delivery timing, or customer segments. | Use for: correlate delivery delays with low review_score; compute average review_score by customer or product (join needed from order_items_enriched); identify orders missing reviews

accepted.name: customer_order_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customer_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders,
  COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_items,
  SUM(oi.price + COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0)) AS total_revenue,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE SUM(oi.price + COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0)) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) END AS average_order_value
FROM orders AS o
LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY o.customer_id
accepted.description: One row per customer_id with aggregated order and spend metrics: total_orders, total_items (count of order_items), total_revenue (sum of price+freight), average_order_value. Useful for RFM, customer lifetime value estimation and segmentation. | Use for: compute customer lifetime revenue and average order value; segment customers by spend or order frequency; join to customer attributes or geolocation for regional analysis

accepted.name: product_category_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders_count,
  COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS items_sold,
  SUM(oi.price + COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0)) AS revenue
FROM order_items AS oi
LEFT JOIN products AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation AS t
  ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
GROUP BY p.product_category_name, t.product_category_name_english
accepted.description: Sales aggregated by product_category_name (category from products) with counts and revenue. Keeps category translation for English label. Useful for category-level performance and trend analysis when joined to time buckets. | Use for: rank categories by revenue or items sold; track category mix over time (join to orders.order_purchase_timestamp); compare category performance across seller regions

accepted.name: seller_location_lookup
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  g.geolocation_lat,
  g.geolocation_lng,
  g.geolocation_city,
  g.geolocation_state
FROM sellers AS s
LEFT JOIN geolocation AS g
  ON s.seller_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: One row per seller_id enriched with geolocation (lat/lng) by matching seller_zip_code_prefix to geolocation rows. Because geolocation may have multiple rows per prefix, this preserves all matching lat/lng points to support spatial aggregations or centroid calculations downstream. | Use for: map seller densities or compute shipping distances; aggregate seller performance by geographic clusters; compute nearest-seller analyses (requires further spatial logic)

accepted.name: orders_latest_status_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_purchase_timestamp DESC) AS purchase_rank
FROM orders
accepted.description: One row per order_id with rank ordering by order_purchase_timestamp (most recent = 1). Useful as a building block for selecting latest orders or recent-order cohorts; exposes purchase_rank so downstream filters can implement top-K or recent-window logic. | Use for: find each customer's most recent order(s); build recency cohorts or compute time-to-repeat metrics; filter to top-N recent orders per customer by WHERE purchase_rank <= N

accepted.name: product_dimensions_normalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  CAST(product_name_lenght AS REAL) AS product_name_lenght,
  CAST(product_description_lenght AS REAL) AS product_description_lenght,
  CAST(product_photos_qty AS REAL) AS product_photos_qty,
  CAST(product_weight_g AS REAL) AS product_weight_g,
  CAST(product_length_cm AS REAL) AS product_length_cm,
  CAST(product_height_cm AS REAL) AS product_height_cm,
  CAST(product_width_cm AS REAL) AS product_width_cm,
  CASE
    WHEN product_length_cm IS NULL OR product_height_cm IS NULL OR product_width_cm IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE COALESCE(product_length_cm,0) * COALESCE(product_height_cm,0) * COALESCE(product_width_cm,0)
  END AS volume_cm3
FROM products
accepted.description: One row per product_id projecting product physical attributes with NULL-preserving casts and derived volumetric measure (volume_cm3). Useful when comparing product sizes/weights or computing shipping estimates. | Use for: estimate shipping cost proxies using weight and volume; filter products by size/weight thresholds for packaging analysis; join product size to order_items to analyze shipping cost by product dimensions

accepted.name: leads_closed_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  lc.mql_id,
  lc.seller_id,
  lc.sdr_id,
  lc.sr_id,
  lc.won_date,
  lc.business_segment,
  lc.lead_type,
  lc.lead_behaviour_profile,
  lc.has_company,
  lc.has_gtin,
  lc.average_stock,
  lc.business_type,
  lc.declared_product_catalog_size,
  lc.declared_monthly_revenue,
  lq.first_contact_date,
  lq.landing_page_id,
  lq.origin
FROM leads_closed AS lc
LEFT JOIN leads_qualified AS lq
  ON lc.mql_id = lq.mql_id
accepted.description: One row per closed lead (leads_closed) enriched with corresponding qualified-lead attributes when available (leads_qualified). Useful for acquisition funnel analysis linking first contact/lead source to closed deals. | Use for: analyze conversion time from first contact to won_date by origin or landing_page_id; segment won leads by business_segment or declared_monthly_revenue; join closed leads to seller performance metrics
